description:
Make storage's read of a repository path at a commit use the git module's object reader instead of libgit2.

## Background

- `JsonFileStorage::read_path_bytes` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1474-1530`) opens libgit2 for a read at a commit (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1492`), resolves the revision and peels it to a commit, and reads the path from its tree. It maps an unresolvable revision to `PathReadError::CommitNotFound`, an absent path to `NotFound` and other failures to `Other`, and labels the result with the commit's first seven hex digits. Working-tree reads use the confined reader.
- Consumers: `CommandExecutor::read_path_bytes` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:840`), `read_document_content` and `read_document_bytes` (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:666`, `crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:700`), `IssueStore::read_path_text` (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:389`), and the server's raw document routes (`crates/server/src/routes.rs:369`, `:685`, `:739`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A read at a commit resolves the commit and reads the path through one object reader on a checkout of the storage's `Git` at the layout's worktree root, and `read_path_bytes` uses no git2.
- [hard] REQ-02: Results and error variants are unchanged: the bytes, the first seven hex digits of the resolved commit, `CommitNotFound` for an unresolvable revision, `NotFound` for an absent path, and `InvalidPath` for a rejected path.
- [hard] REQ-03: The existing `read_path_bytes` tests and the server document API tests pass, and a unit test reads a binary file and an absent path at a commit of a real repository.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Path reads at a commit go through the git module
